title: Why Honey Never Goes Bad (Even After Thousands of Years)

scenes.text: There's a food in your kitchen that can't go bad. Ever.
Archaeologists have opened pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs. Thousands of years old, and still perfectly preserved.
Most food rots because bacteria move in. Honey gives them nowhere to live.
It's almost all sugar with very little water, and it's acidic, with a pH around four. Bacteria simply dry out and die.
And bees add one more trick. An enzyme in their stomach makes tiny amounts of hydrogen peroxide, a natural disinfectant.
Keep the lid sealed and your honey could outlive you. What's the oldest thing in your pantry?

description:
Honey is the one food in your kitchen that never goes bad. Archaeologists have found pots of it in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old and still preserved.
It's almost all sugar with very little water, it's acidic with a pH around 4, and bees add an enzyme that makes a little hydrogen peroxide. Bacteria can't survive in it.
Keep the lid sealed and it lasts for centuries.
What's the oldest thing in your pantry?
